title: Allow chezmoi rendering without bash.d
description: On hosts without access to the private Adyen bash.d repository, chezmoi status and initialization fail because dot_config/bead-dispatcher/config.yaml.tmpl unconditionally includes ~/.bash.d/bead-dispatcher-config.yaml. Make bash.d and dependent generated files optional while preserving current behavior when the external exists.
acceptance_criteria: With HOME pointing to a temporary directory that has no .bash.d, chezmoi can render/status the dotfiles source without an include error; when bead-dispatcher-config.yaml exists, its contents are still rendered with the source-file placeholder replaced.
close_reason: Made bash.d optional across Chezmoi external management, target selection, and defensive rendering; added clean-home and existing-bash.d regression coverage.

title: Adopt chezmoi framework for dotfiles management
design:
## Current State
- Two custom Python symlink scripts (symlink.py ~50 lines, symlink_dotfiles.py ~150 lines) requiring Python + watchdog, loguru, jinja2, pyyaml
- Jinja2 templating via ~/.config/alex.conf (YAML variables file)
- Rendered output to dist/ directory, then symlinked to ~/
- Nix/Home Manager (flake.nix, home.nix) for package management on 4 hosts (alex, mu, alpha, alpha-windows)
- Shell bootstrap scripts (setup, setup_lite, scripts/) chaining 5 scripts together
- No secret management or encryption for dotfiles
- No dry-run/diff capability before applying changes
- symlink_dotfiles.py has --watch mode for auto-re-render on file changes

## Migration Plan
1. Install chezmoi and run chezmoi init to create source directory (~/.local/share/chezmoi)
2. Add dotfiles with chezmoi add (e.g., ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.tmux.conf, ~/.vimrc, ~/.taskrc, etc.)
3. Convert files needing per-host logic to templates with chezmoi add --template (replaces Jinja2 templating from alex.conf)
4. Move bootstrap scripts to chezmoi run_once_ scripts (run_once_bootstrap.sh, run_once_nix.sh, run_once_homemanager.sh, run_once_nvim.sh)
5. Keep flake.nix/home.nix as-is — invoked via run_once_ scripts (chezmoi and Home Manager are orthogonal, not competing)
6. Add secret management: integrate with password manager (1Password/Bitwarden/pass) for any tokens/API keys in dotfiles
7. Delete symlink.py, symlink_dotfiles.py, dist/, setup, setup_lite, and related Python deps (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .venv)
8. Update .gitignore and README accordingly

## What chezmoi Replaces
- symlink.py (plain symlinking) → chezmoi add (writes files or manages symlinks)
- symlink_dotfiles.py (Jinja2 templating + watch) → chezmoi Go text/template with auto OS/hostname variables
- ~/.config/alex.conf (YAML vars) → chezmoi .chezmoidata.yaml or .chezmoidata.toml
- dist/ directory → no longer needed (chezmoi renders directly)
- setup / setup_lite scripts → chezmoi init --apply (single command bootstrap)

## What chezmoi Does NOT Replace
- flake.nix / home.nix (Nix Home Manager) — keep as-is, run via chezmoi run_once_ script
- bin/ directory (utility scripts) — keep as-is
- scripts/ directory (operational scripts) — move relevant ones to chezmoi run_once_/run_onchange_, keep rest

## Caveats
- Go text/template is less featureful than Jinja2 (no filters like |default, different whitespace handling). Most dotfiles won't need complex templates.
- No built-in file watching (replaces symlink_dotfiles.py --watch). Workflow shifts to: chezmoi edit → chezmoi apply.
- chezmoi source naming conventions take getting used to (dot_ prefix for dotfiles, .tmpl suffix for templates).
- Need to learn chezmoi add/edit/apply/re-apply workflow.

## Key chezmoi Benefits
1. Zero-dependency single binary (no Python venv required)
2. Built-in secret management via password managers (1Password, Bitwarden, pass, KeePassXC, macOS Keychain, etc.)
3. Per-file encryption via age/gpg
4. Dry-run and diff before applying (chezmoi diff, chezmoi apply --dry-run)
5. Atomic file updates (no broken symlinks on interruption)
6. Single-command bootstrap on new machines
7. run_once_ scripts replace bootstrap orchestration
8. Automatic OS/hostname/arch detection in templates
acceptance_criteria:
1. All current dotfiles managed by chezmoi (chezmoi list shows them)
2. Templated files render correctly on all 4 hosts (alex, mu, alpha, alpha-windows)
3. Secret management configured (password manager integration or age encryption for sensitive files)
4. Bootstrap on fresh machine works with: chezmoi init --apply <github-username>
5. flake.nix and home.nix still work via chezmoi run_once_ scripts
6. symlink.py, symlink_dotfiles.py, dist/, and Python deps removed
7. chezmoi diff and chezmoi apply --dry-run work correctly
8. No functionality lost from current setup
close_reason: Migrated dotfiles from custom Python symlink scripts to chezmoi. All acceptance criteria met.
